channel.title: CTV News – Queen's Park
channel.description: Queen's Park coverage from CTV News Toronto.

item.title: What elected trustees at supervised school boards can and can’t do, according to this memo
Ontario won’t make career college OSAP audit public, minister says
item.description: Ontario’s colleges and universities minister said Tuesday he will not be releasing a government-commissioned audit into student financial aid usage at career colleges.

item.title: Thousands of OSAP applications came from a single IP address, ministry alleges
item.description: At two career colleges now under the Ontario government’s microscope, more than half of the thousands of student financial aid applications last year came from a single IP address, officials allege in documents filed in court.

item.title: Toronto cyclists protest Ontario's bike lane removals at Queen's Park
item.description: Dozens of cycling advocates and protesters spent their Halloween decrying Ontario’s contentious decision to continue removing bike lanes across Toronto.

item.title: Ontario deficit grows to $16.9 billion as trade war with U.S. drags on
item.description: Ontario’s deficit has grown by more than $3 billion in the past few months as the province continues to face economic headwinds blowing up from the U.S.

item.title: Assault charges dropped against Sault MPP
item.description: More than a year after Sault Ste. Marie MPP Chris Scott was charged with two counts of assault, the case was dropped Wednesday.

item.title: Ontario environment minister hopes to burn more garbage for energy, build more landfills
item.description: Ontario’s environment minister hopes to burn more garbage for energy and build more landfills as the province runs out of space to dump its trash and is framing it as a way to fight U.S. President Donald Trump’s recent tariff on Canadian trash.

item.title: Ontario pauses some skills training funding for unemployed people: career colleges
item.description: In addition to freezing Ontario Student Assistance Program payments to all private post-secondary institutions, the province has paused at least some funding through Better Jobs Ontario. But the government won’t explicitly say so.

item.title: Ontario matches feds' tax perk for businesses on capital investments
item.description: Ontario is matching the federal government’s recent move to give businesses a tax break on capital investments.

item.title: Ford says he feels ‘terrible’ for honest students caught in career college OSAP pause
item.description: Ontario Premier Doug Ford said Tuesday he feels “terrible” for honest students caught up in a career college system where financial aid is now unavailable, but opposition leaders say the students are only in that situation because of him.

item.title: Former Ontario cabinet minister who resigned over expenses scandal defends promotion
item.description: A former member of Ontario Premier Doug Ford’s cabinet who resigned his post over an expenses scandal is defending his recent promotion.

item.title: Timeline of events in OSAP career colleges warnings, probes
item.description: Ontario Premier Doug Ford’s government is coming under increasing fire for how it has handled Ontario Student Assistance Program payments at private career colleges.

item.title: Ontario attaches more than 511K people to primary care amid goal of connecting all
item.description: Ontario Health Minister Sylvia Jones says more than 511,000 people have been connected to primary care since her government set a goal of attaching everyone in the province.

item.title: OSAP, affordability questions likely to dominate as Queen's Park resumes sitting
item.description: Provincial politicians are returning to the Ontario legislature Tuesday for the first time in 21 weeks with some new faces thanks to three byelections, a rejigged cabinet and a new cloud of scandal hanging over the government’s head.

item.title: Ontario is planning to launch digital IDs. Here’s what you need to know.
item.description: The Ford government says it plans to launch digital credentials, starting with the Ontario Photo Card and then later expanding to driver’s licences and health cards.
